subject.gist: A miniature artist and her filmmaker husband made room for work and gardens on a narrow plot, gradually growing comfortable with their home’s wear.

story.text: A miniature artist and her husband, who directs commercials, make a narrow Tokyo plot into a place where work, favourite objects and greenery are all close at hand. Her studio and gallery fill the little gatehouse, with his study above; a courtyard leads to their home behind. Lowering the bedroom and bathroom to meet the height limit brings another pleasure: lying down puts the garden at eye level, as though they are resting in the grass. The house need not stay pristine. As its surfaces wear and belongings settle in, she feels increasingly at home, growing closer to the building rather than worrying about keeping it new.

claims.text: The household is in Tokyo, Japan.
Plot narrows to 2 meters [6.56 feet].
Masahiro and Mao Harada designed the home.
Gatehouse combines entryway, art gallery and offices.
Lower floor was sunk to meet the building-height limit.
The site is subject to a strict building-height limit.
Building codes limit the home’s height.
Inheriting land in Japan incurs a large inheritance tax.
Owners subdivide and sell land to pay inheritance tax.
Inheritance taxes encourage plots to be divided and sold.
The shelf uprights form structural framing.
Structural uprights are 30 mm [3 cm] thick.
Walls and floors have MDF interior finishes.
The interior finish uses MDF.
Lower gatehouse serves as the resident’s studio and gallery.
claims.doubt: The captions do not label the voices during the gallery introduction; the later first-person workspace statement is from an unnamed resident.

claims.text: Upper gatehouse is the husband’s study.
The resident’s husband directs commercials.
A small wooden ladder accesses the upper study.
claims.doubt: The description says wooden, but the reviewed frames show a gray metallic-looking round-rung ladder.

claims.text: Plant pockets were added to an old fence.
The kitchen is part of the living room.
The concealed lower appliance is a microwave.
The slatted cabinet conceals an air conditioner.
The small structural members are inexpensive.
The small structural members can be carried by hand.
Construction did not require large building machinery.
Japanese craftsmen made the building by hand.
The paper and wood materials can return to earth.
The design accepts aging and dirt positively.
The resident is in her fifth year with the house.
claims.doubt: The machine translation says five years, while the original Japanese auto-captions say 今5年目, meaning now in the fifth year.
